differentiation.occupancy_preservation: The KL term moves codewords so the source's soft assignment distribution approaches the target-derived distribution, encouraging behaviour-aligned repartitioning rather than directly pulling the pair's two nearest codewords together. The mass-preservation penalty discourages behaviour weighting from changing aggregate assignment mass relative to the unweighted source assignments. It does not mathematically guarantee unchanged hard cell sizes or pairwise codeword separation; it avoids an explicit pair-convergence objective.

vs_r8.why: It reaches the codebook, unlike the inert encoder-only arms. It acts on directed assignment distributions and aggregate assignment mass rather than applying pairwise cross-entropy that makes both endpoints share a codeword, so it does not explicitly reward pair convergence or cell merging. Its soft marginal constraint is only a hypothesis about preserving the hard partition and must be checked on the cold export.

differentiation.vs_reference_arm: the reference arm is the untouched host; this candidate adds one term whose gradient reaches the codebook without pulling a transition's two codewords together

equation: For each valid ordered pair i, define p_i(j) = softmax_j(-||s_i-c_j||^2 / tau) and q_i(j) = softmax_j(-||t_i-c_j||^2 / tau). Define the directed target distribution r_i(j) = softmax_j(-||t_i-c_j||^2 / tau). Minimize L = w * mean_i[m_i * KL(r_i || p_i)] + eta * sum_j (u_j - v_j)^2, where m_i = sigmoid((||s_i-c_{k_i}||^2 - ||t_i-c_{l_i}||^2) / tau), u_j = mean_i[m_i * p_i(j)], and v_j = mean_i[p_i(j)].
expected_failure_modes: The soft transport and aggregate mass penalty may preserve only soft marginal usage while hard nearest-code assignments still lose codes, concentrate cells, narrow prefix branches, or drift between train and test. Also, because target-derived assignments can be ambiguous, the term may improve soft alignment without increasing hard pair-level ER.

forbidden_substitutions.reason: a quota on the assignment is the family that produced 39.5% and 24.2% occupancy without preserving the exported codes
a term that pulls a pair's two codewords together is what collapsed the level-0 codebook to two codes

hypotheses: The candidate is wrong if a cold export does not raise frozen ER while meeting every structural requirement: level-0 codes in use at least control, Gini no higher than control, L1-to-L2 branches at least control, no increased train-to-test frequency drift, and sequence information no lower than control. A codebook gradient that is zero or non-finite, or a loss unchanged by exchanging source and target, also falsifies the proposal.

symbols.KL(a || b): Kullback-Leibler divergence from distribution a to distribution b.
symbols.c_j: Codeword j in the supplied codebook.
symbols.eta: Strength of the assignment-mass preservation penalty.
symbols.k_i: Nearest-codeword index for s_i, used only to define the directed weight.
symbols.l_i: Nearest-codeword index for t_i, used only to define the directed weight.
symbols.m_i: Directed weight, larger when the target's nearest-codeword distance is smaller than the source's.
symbols.p_i(j): Soft source assignment probability to codeword j.
symbols.q_i(j): Soft target assignment probability to codeword j; included to specify the target-side soft assignment.
symbols.r_i(j): Target-derived desired assignment distribution over codewords.
symbols.u_j: Behaviour-weighted mean source assignment mass for codeword j.
symbols.v_j: Unweighted mean source assignment mass for codeword j.

tests.statement: the term's value on a hand-computable case matches the declared equation
